headline: Amazon introduces grocery discount for US employees from 1 October
summary: Starting October 1, Amazon is launching an ongoing grocery discount for all US employees across its corporate, fulfillment, and retail operations. The benefit provides staff with a 10% discount on online Amazon and Whole Foods purchases, alongside a 20% discount for in-store shopping at Whole Foods and Daily Shop locations. The perk is part of a broader $230 million investment aimed at expanding pay and benefits across the company's workforce.

headline: India accounts for 20% of global chip-design workforce: Intel Report
summary: India now represents approximately 20% of the global chip design and VLSI workforce, backed by over 85,000 specialized skill sets developed over the last four years. Educational initiatives across more than 355 universities and a growing deep-tech startup ecosystem are strengthening the local engineering pipeline to meet rising AI-driven computing demands. This talent expansion supports India's strategic push to increase its role in the global semiconductor value chain.

headline: Maple India appoints Farhan Qureshi as group head-HR
summary: Maple India has appointed Farhan Qureshi as its new Group Head of Human Resources, tasking him with leading HR strategy and operations across the organization's brands, stores, and corporate entities. Qureshi brings over 13 years of HR leadership experience across retail, luxury, and consumer-facing sectors, having previously served in senior roles at Burgundy Brand Collective, Novel Jewels, and Reliance Retail. He holds an MBA in HR Management from Guru Nanak Institute of Management Studies.

headline: Rising Star: Hiral Patel
summary: Hiral Patel, a finalist for the HRKatha Rising Star Leadership Award 2025, advocates for a relationship-driven approach to human resources at Reliance Industries. After transitioning from learning and development into manufacturing HR, he focuses on understanding core business operations while building trust by recognizing employees' life contexts beyond the workplace. By connecting talent and retention strategies directly to operational outcomes, Patel aligns HR initiatives with broader business goals.

headline: Swiggy puts earnings in partners’ hands
summary: Swiggy has launched an 'Early Cashout' feature that allows its network of over 6.5 lakh delivery partners to access their earned income within an hour rather than waiting for standard weekly payouts. Available across more than 720 cities, the initiative was developed in response to worker feedback seeking greater financial flexibility for daily and emergency expenses. The instant payout model reflects a broader effort by on-demand platforms to boost gig worker satisfaction and retention.

headline: The office phrases that should probably retire
summary: HR executives argue that overused corporate phrases like 'give me two minutes' and 'low-hanging fruit' substitute the appearance of progress for genuine commitment. Instead of relying on vague shorthand, leaders recommend using precise timelines and specific questions to drive accountability and actionable results. Replacing clichés with clear language improves workplace efficiency and helps teams better plan their time.

headline: 80 jobs lost suddenly in five-minute Google Meet call
summary: US-based fintech firm Bluevine abruptly laid off its 80-member Indian customer support team during a five-minute virtual meeting. While management attributed the decision to underperformance, former employees contested the claims, citing high output and lack of prior warning. The incident underscores the precarity of outsourced roles and offshore human resource management within global corporations.

headline: Priyadarshi Bhattacharya is MD, global HR head-group tech, strategy & transformation, and APAC, Swiss Re
summary: Swiss Re has promoted Priyadarshi Bhattacharya to Managing Director and Global Head of HR for group technology, strategy & transformation, and APAC. Based in Zurich, Bhattacharya originally joined the reinsurer in 2020 following prior HR leadership roles at financial institutions including HSBC, ANZ, and DBS Bank. In his expanded position, he will oversee global people strategy across digital and technology divisions while driving HR performance across the APAC region.

headline: Innoviti Technologies appoints Ramdas Parameswaran as CFO
summary: Innoviti Technologies has appointed Ramdas Parameswaran as its new Chief Financial Officer to lead its finance, legal, compliance, and administrative functions. Parameswaran brings over 20 years of experience from major consumer and tech firms, including PepsiCo, Flipkart, and ACKO Life Insurance. In his new role, he will focus on driving sustainable, profitable growth and refining the company's product roadmap as Innoviti turns profitable.

headline: 76% employees say AI could encourage them to use more PTO: Study
summary: A recent study by Zoom reveals that 76% of workers would take more paid time off if AI reliably assisted with post-vacation catch-up tasks. Backlog anxiety currently leads many employees, particularly managers and Gen Z, to leave leave unused or monitor emails while away. Consequently, 76% of IT decision-makers plan to invest in productivity and work-continuity technologies over the coming year to address these workplace disruptions.

headline: Relaxo launches intra-company cricket tournament to strengthen employee engagement
summary: Footwear manufacturer Relaxo has launched the Relaxo Premier League, an internal cricket tournament designed to boost employee engagement and cross-functional collaboration. The inaugural competition brings together 120 employees from corporate, warehouse, and manufacturing units across six teams in New Delhi. Running through November, the initiative focuses on building camaraderie, teamwork, and physical fitness among staff.

headline: Adidas trims tech roles in India, less than 20% impacted
summary: Adidas is restructuring its India Technology Hub in Gurugram, impacting less than 20% of its local tech workforce. Affected employees were either issued immediate exit notices or asked to remain through December to assist with knowledge transfer and seek internal redeployment. The company stated the realignment supports its long-term business strategy while reaffirming India's ongoing strategic importance.

headline: Radio ad volumes rise 1.2% in Jan-Jul 2026: TAM AdEx
summary: Radio advertising volumes grew by 1.2% during January-July 2026, led by the services sector and strong growth in real estate category advertising. Maruti Suzuki India and LIC of India emerged as the top individual advertisers during the period, while Vimal Pan Masala was the leading brand. Regionally, Gujarat and Jaipur captured the highest shares of ad volumes, with evening slots and 20-to-40 second ads remaining the most preferred formats.

headline: 91% of India’s Next Gen pays more attention to funny brands: Snapchat-Omnicom study
summary: A joint study by Snapchat and Omnicom Advertising reveals that 91% of India's Gen Z and Gen Alpha pay closer attention to brands that use humor effectively. While humorous marketing significantly boosts purchase consideration and word-of-mouth recommendations, 80% of young consumers feel online brand jokes often seem forced or out of touch. Consequently, experts advise companies to deeply understand cultural contexts and embrace authentic self-deprecation rather than simply copying online trends.

headline: Bhavna Verma concludes five-year stint at Hindustan Unilever
summary: Bhavna Verma has stepped down from her role as Global Brand Director for POND’S, concluding a five-year tenure at Hindustan Unilever. During her time with the company, she led brand strategy, innovation, and campaign modernizations for legacy products following an earlier eight-year stint at Reckitt. Verma has not yet disclosed details regarding her next professional move.

These approaches allow homeowners and designers to blend practical daily needs seamlessly into the room's overall architecture.
